decision_note: Two-population Primula secundiflora study estimates pollinator-mediated selection under different pollinator assemblages; nectar-hole-using bumblebees are treated as pollinating visitors and the abstract does not identify a separate plant-antagonist fitness channel.

Review directly synthesizes molecular mechanisms and natural selection on flower-colour variation, including pollinator and non-pollinator selective agents; retain as relevant synthesis/source-chasing material, not as a primary held-out programme.

Cornell dissertation explicitly concerns variation, agents and consequences of natural selection on floral traits; retain conservatively to resolve primary chapters, antagonist channels and dependence on later Penstemon publications.

Two-population Silene littorea study estimates phenotypic selection and path structure on floral colour/traits while explicitly assessing herbivory, male/female fitness and among-population variation; retain for repeated-context estimand adjudication.

Three-population Primula farinosa study links morph-specific pollen limitation, grazer/seed-predator damage and phenotypic selection on flower number, petal size and corolla-tube width; retain for source-level dependence and repeated-context adjudication.

Ipomopsis aggregata field experiment crosses snowmelt timing with summer precipitation over three years and quantifies selection on floral volatiles/morphology through pollination, seed-predator escape and total seed production; retain as a high-value repeated-context estimand candidate.
